title: Ultrafiltration System

introduction.definition: An ultrafiltration system pumps water through pressurised modules packed with hollow fibres with very fine pores. Water and dissolved salts pass through; suspended solids, colloids, bacteria and most viruses are held back. Short backwashes with filtrate restore flux every 20–60 minutes.
applications: Industrial process water and wastewater reuse

pressure.title: Moderate trans-membrane pressure
pressure.description: UF modules typically run at a trans-membrane pressure of roughly 0.2–2 bar. Water and dissolved salts pass; suspended solids, colloids, bacteria and most viruses are retained. Every 20–60 min a short backwash (and sometimes chemically enhanced backwash) restores the flux.

video_tutorials.title: Ultrafiltration System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Ultrafiltration System.
An ultrafiltration system pumps water through pressurised modules packed with hollow fibres with very fine pores.
Water and dissolved salts pass through; suspended solids, colloids, bacteria and most viruses are held back.
Short backwashes with filtrate restore flux every 20–60 minutes.
Typical applications include drinking-water treatment; pre-treatment before reverse osmosis; industrial process water and wastewater reuse.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: UF Modules (pressure housings), Feed Pump, Feed Pump — Shaft & Coupling (turning), Backwash Pump.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Ultrafiltration System — Operation

script.narration: How the Ultrafiltration System works.
The feed pump supplies water through the strainer.
Water enters the modules and passes through the fibres.
Filtrate collects in the top header and tank.
Periodically the backwash pump reverses flow to clean the fibres.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
UF modules typically run at a trans-membrane pressure of roughly 0.2–2 bar.

video_tutorials.title: Ultrafiltration System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Ultrafiltration System.
Trend TMP and permeability.
Pressure-decay integrity test.
Recovery CIP; replace modules.
Watch for integrity failure: pressure-decay test fails. Common cause: broken fibres.
Watch for irreversible fouling: low permeability after cleaning. Common cause: organics, iron/manganese.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
